catalog_quote: [p.120, 2.63] a) C'est un accent de hauteur. En sangu, c'est la hauteur et non l'intensité de la voix qui fait contraster le segment accentué par rapport à ceux qui ne le sont pas. ... La différence phonologique entre les deux formes d'accent se ramène à ce que l'un est senti comme frappant la syllabe entière (accent d'intensité, comme en allemand et en russe), alors que l'autre ne frappe que la partie vocalique de la syllabe, là où justement l'élément de hauteur est plus important, (accent de hauteur comme en serbo-croate) [p.123, §3] Le sangu est une langue à accent, et non à tons. [p.118, 2.62] L'unité accentuable en sangu n'est pas la syllabe, mais la more. [p.134, 2.81] Dans les monèmes invariables et les formes nominales et pronominales, l'accent en sangu peut avoir l'une des trois positions suivantes: a) sur la more antépénultième, b) sur la more pénultième, c) sur la more précédant immédiatement le radical. Le premier cas est de beaucoup le plus fréquent. Sur une liste de 600 mots, nous en avons comptés 540 qui avaient ainsi l'accent sur la more antépénultième. [p.139, 2.86] Les syntagmes verbaux portent tous l'accent sur la more antépénultième, à moins que cet accent ne soit avancé d'une ou deux mores comme il sera expliqué en B (2.89 - 2.99)

new_statements.translation: [p.134] In invariable monemes and in nominal and pronominal forms, the accent in Sangu can have one of the following three positions: a) on the antepenultimate mora, b) on the penultimate mora, c) on the mora immediately preceding the radical. The first case is by far the most frequent. In a list of 600 words we counted 540 which had the accent on the antepenultimate mora. [p.139] Verbal syntagms (verb forms) all carry the accent on the antepenultimate mora, unless this accent is advanced by one or two morae as will be explained in B (2.89-2.99).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sangu is analysed as an accent (not tone) language with one pitch accent per word, counted in morae: by default the accent falls on the antepenultimate mora of the word (90% of non-verbal forms; all verb forms and infinitives). Because long vowels count two morae, a word with a long penultimate vowel carries the accent inside the penultimate syllable (kitaana, kiidepa), otherwise on the antepenultimate syllable (umugosi, kijova). The accent is realised as higher pitch ('accent de hauteur'), with falling or rising contour on long vowels.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; each accentual unit (form) carries a single accent (2.60-2.61).
new_statements.exceptions: Non-verbals: a lexical class with accent on the penultimate mora -- all forms of only two morae, all forms whose last syllable is CwV/CyV, plus listed nouns (2.83-2.84, e.g. umutwa, iimbwa, indama) -- and a class with accent on the mora immediately before the radical (radicals of three or more morae, e.g. ilijevele, inkweembe; 2.85). Verbs: accent advanced one mora toward the end by passive -w- or causative -y-, or by a class 1/class 9 subject prefix combined with a past or perfect, or by negation combined with past/perfect/injunctive/dubitative; advanced two morae (onto the final mora) when conditions from both categories co-occur (2.89-2.99). Functional items (connective -a etc.) form one accentual unit with the following word (2.61).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = the 'unite accentuelle', i.e. each nominal, pronominal or verbal form (word), with proclitic functionals joining the following form; accent-bearing unit = mora (2.62); citation forms and texts are marked consistently. Heese 1919-20 (p.88) heard the same facts as 'main accent on the first stem syllable / perfects penultimate / monosyllabic stems on the prefix' (his examples are all antepenultimate-mora); Kaajan 2012 re-analyses them as a restricted tone system with H on the antepenultimate mora (penultimate with cl.1/9 subjects in a-/-ile paradigms). In syllable terms the rule is quantity-sensitive (long penult attracts the accent), so 'weight-sensitive' or 'pitch accent' are defensible alternative codings.
new_statements.identity_note: All three sources describe the same language, Sangu/Kisangu of the Usangu plains (Mbarali District, Mbeya Region), Guthrie G61, glottocode sang1330 -- not Sango of the CAR (sang1328) nor Sangu of Gabon. Heese 1919-20 writes 'Sango' (Berlin Mission station Brandt in Usangu); Bilodeau 1979 worked on the plains variety in the 1970s; Kaajan 2012 is based on the central (Utengule) variety and notes North/East/West/South-Central dialects (Mitterhofer & Smith 2008).

new_statements.quote: [p.148, sec.40] Über den Accent ist zu sagen, dass derselbe meist auf der Stammsilbe steht. (Die Einsilbigen haben den Ton auf der vorletzten, dem Präfix.) Hat die vorletzte Silbe aber einen durch Kontraktion entstandenen Vokal, so erhält dieser den Accent. Hat die Endsilbe den hohen Ton, so bleibt der Accent doch auf der Stammsilbe. Die Töne sind im Sa. sehr wichtig. Die sämtlichen mit ya gebildeten Kausative haben den hohen Ton auf der Endsilbe, ebenso ihre Perfekta, s. 38, c, 2. [p.133, sec.7 Bem.] Die Vokale lauten in der Tonsilbe lang, auch vor folgendem nasaliertem Konsonanten, sonst kurz.
new_statements.translation: [p.148, sec.40] About the accent it should be said that it mostly stands on the stem syllable. (Monosyllabic [stems] have the accent on the penultimate, the prefix.) But if the penultimate syllable has a vowel that arose by contraction, that vowel receives the accent. If the final syllable has the high tone, the accent nevertheless stays on the stem syllable. The tones are very important in Sango. All causatives formed with ya have the high tone on the final syllable, as do their perfects, see 38, c, 2. [p.133] The vowels are long in the accented syllable, also before a following nasalised consonant, otherwise short.

Meinhof adds a morphological formulation (stem syllable), the contraction rule and vowel lengthening under accent, and he treats tone as a separate, 'very important' system (final high tone on ya-causatives/perfects), which sides with the catalo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent (kept distinct from tone) falls on the (first) syllable of the stem; with a monosyllabic stem it falls on the preceding prefix, i.e. the penult; a penultimate vowel produced by contraction (e.g. perfects valála > valéle, vonéye) attracts the accent; the accented syllable's vowel is lengthened. Separately, Sango has significant tones: ya-causatives and their perfects carry a high tone on the final syllable, and a final high tone does not move the accent off the stem syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: monosyllabic stems (accent on the prefix = penult); contraction vowels in the penult attract the accent (perfects of derived verbs, p.146 sec.38 c 2: 'Dieser durch Kontraktion entstandene Vokal zieht den Accent auf sich, waehrend bei den Perfekten der einfachen Verba der Accent auf der Stammsilbe bleibt'); high tone on the final syllable of ya-causatives and their perfects.
new_statements.identity_note: Meinhof's 'Sango (Sa.)' = 'die Sprache der Sango oder Wa-loli in Deutsch-Ostafrika, noerdlich vom Nyassa', capital Utengule, chief Merere; data from Th. Richard (Herrnhut Moravian mission, Utengule); he notes the subjugated Safwa also speak Sango. This is Sangu [sbp], sang1330 (not Ubangian Sango).

sources.note: p.88 'Die Akzente': author could not establish good practical rules; tendency to put the main accent as far as possible on the first stem syllable (umukwamidzi < -kwamila, umugosi < -gosi); all verbal perfect endings have the main accent on the penultimate syllable; nouns with monosyllabic stems shift the accent to the last prefix syllable (umutwe). Accents marked throughout the article.
